answer: Agents exchanging orchard sensor data about nectar yields use prepaid byte-for-byte exchange: a requester must first deliver a useful, previously unseen data chunk verified against the buyer's sensor registry. The buyer credits its measured size once and atomically debits credit before serving data; new accounts start at zero. Hollow identities gain no free downloads, and replaying chunks across aliases earns no extra credit. This limits sybil freeloading, provided usefulness and source authenticity can be checked.
